title: Structured Output: the AI's answer as a C# type
why: In lecture 2 the model's answer was free text — “almost” exact with a prompt (even with few-shot). But “almost” isn't enough for code: `if (label == "Negative")` needs the exact value. Today we force the model to return a C# type instead of text: an enum or an object that goes straight into our logic. This is the bridge between a user's free text and our code.
outcomes: Drive code with a typed answer (Negative → notify the manager) and tell `response.Result` from `response.Text`
Get an enum with `GetResponseAsync<T>` and explain why it's more reliable than a prompt (even with examples)
Extract an object from text with a `record`: nullable fields, `Description`, today's date in the prompt
Explain why the shape is guaranteed but the content is not, and check the received object in C#

review.q: Why do we return `response.Result.ToString()` and not `response.Text`?
review.a: `Text` is the model's raw JSON: `{"data": "Negative"}` · the typed value lives only in `Result` · `ToString()` → `"Negative"`, so the API client doesn't get a number (`1`)

review.q: In `FeedbackController`, what does the code do on a Negative review? Why do we need an enum for it?
review.a: `Console.WriteLine("SMS: notify the manager")` — in a real system an SMS/notification service · `if (response.Result == Sentiment.Negative)` always works, because no value outside the schema can come back; with text (`Negative.`) it would fail

review.q: How does few-shot differ from structured output?
review.a: Few-shot **asks** for a shape with examples — by probability · structured output **forces** it: a JSON Schema from the C# type goes with the request, the model can't write outside the schema, `.Result` is already a C# type

review.q: Why `int? Guests` and not `int` in `BookingParseResponse`? And why do we put today's date in the prompt?
review.a: `?` gives the model the right to say “I don't know” (null); with `int` it's forced to write something and will make it up · the model doesn't know today's date (stateless, training date) — we provide it for “tomorrow”

review.q: Structured output gave us a `BookingParseResponse`. Can we write it straight to the database?
review.a: No · the shape is guaranteed, the content isn't: “23:30” → a valid object, but we're closed; the guests are missing (null) · C# checks and returns a 400 with a question for the guest

quiz.q: The prompt-based classify sometimes returns `Search.`. Why doesn't this happen with `GetResponseAsync<RequestType>`?
options: The JSON Schema goes with the request and the model can't choose a token outside the schema
quiz.explain: A prompt asks for a shape, structured output forces it. The allowed values are in the schema, and the model chooses only among them.

quiz.q: The endpoint returns `Ok(response.Result)` where `Result` = `Sentiment.Mixed`. What do we see in Swagger?
options: `2` — by default ASP.NET Core returns an enum as a number
quiz.explain: That's why on the slide we return `sentiment.ToString()`. The alternative is `JsonStringEnumConverter` in `Program.cs`.

quiz.q: If `FeedbackController` returned `Ok(response.Text)`, what would we see in Swagger?
quiz.explain: `Text` is the text of the model's answer, and with structured output that's JSON with a wrapper. The typed value is in `Result`, hence `response.Result.ToString()`.

quiz.q: “There are four of us, tomorrow at 8” — why do we write `Today is {DateTime.Now:…}` in the system prompt?
options: The answer is faster that way
The model doesn't know today's date — we provide it so it can work out “tomorrow”
Gemini returns an error without a date
It's part of the JSON Schema
quiz.explain: The model is stateless and its knowledge stops at its training date. Today's date is context we provide — with the lecture 2 prompt template.

quiz.q: Structured output returned a `BookingParseResponse`. What is guaranteed?
options: That the answer has the shape of `BookingDetails`; C# has to check the values
That `At` is always within opening hours
quiz.explain: The shape is guaranteed, the content is not: “at 8” may become 08:00, a field may be null. C# checks before the database.

quiz.q: In a structured output prompt, is it better to write “return JSON with fields at and guests”?
options: No — the schema is sent with the request anyway; in the prompt we write what to extract and by which rules
Yes, otherwise the model can't write JSON
quiz.explain: Google recommends not repeating the schema in the prompt — it lowers quality. The schema sets the shape, the prompt sets the rules (e.g. “leave null whatever is not in the text”).
